##### **1.2.1.1 Package Description**

| No | Package | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 01 | API | Exposes endpoints, contains middleware, helpers, real-time hubs, and services. |
| 02 | CouchDb.Domain | Defines CouchDB entities, enums. |
| 03 | Domain | Defines core business entities, enums, and exceptions. |
| 04 | Repositories | Contains CouchDB repositories |
| 05 | Services | Business logic layer, including interfaces, implementations. |
| 06 | Controllers | Handles HTTP requests and routes to services. |
| 07 | Consumers | Contains consumer classes responding to messages from RabbitMQ. |
| 08 | Middlewares | Pipeline components for request/response handling. |
| 09 | Constants | Define shared constants for API endpoints, header keys used across controllers. |
| 10 | ExternalClients | Contains HTTP client classes responsible for handling communication with external cloud systems. |
| 11 | DTOs | Contains all data transfer objects used in the system |
| 12 | BackgroundServices | Contains host background services that monitor and react to changes in CouchDB, enabling asynchronous and publish message events.. |
| 13 | Utils | Utility functions to support operations. |
| 14 | Converters | Contains classes for transforming input data into desired output formats. |
| 15 | Enums | Enumerations representing fixed value sets. |
| 16 | CustomExceptions | Defines system error models and error codes. |
| 17 | Shared.MessageStore | Defines system event messages, exchange names, queue names, and routing keys for each queue used in message-based communication.  |

##### **1.2.2.1 Package Description**

| 3 | APIs.Mappers | Define mapping rules between entities and DTOs (Data Transfer Objects). |
| 4 | APIs.Middlewares | Includes middlewares for the system. |
| 5 | APIs.Constants | Defines reusable system-wide constants. |
| 6 | APIs.Attributes | Custom attributes for validation, authorization, and metadata. |
| 7 | APIs.Extensions | Extension methods to support controller logic or service registration. |
| 8 | Domains | Represents the core domain logic including entities, enums, and DbContext. |
| 9 | Domains.Context | Contains the DbContext and EF Core configurations. |
| 10 | Domains.Enums | Defines all enum types used across the system). |
| 11 | Domains.Models | Entity classes that represent tables in the database. |
| 12 | Domains.Pagination | Includes pagination-related models and helpers. |
| 13 | Repositories | Data Access Layer that defines and implements data queries and persistence. |
| 14 | Repositories.Interfaces | Repository interfaces for entity access. |
| 15 | Repositories.Implements | Concrete implementations of repository interfaces. |
| 16 | Services | Contains business logic services and integrations with external/internal systems. |
| 17 | Services.AzureIotHubClient | Handles communication with Azure IoT Hub for device control and updates. |
| 18 | Services.BackgroundJobs | Background job handlers using Hangfire (e.g. syncing, device checks). |
| 19 | Services.Base | Common base classes shared by services. |
| 20 | Services.CapRabbitMQ | Integration with RabbitMQ using CAP for event publishing and subscribing. |

| 25 | Services.Interfaces | Interfaces that define service contracts. |

| 28 | Services.VNPayClient | VNPay payment integration |
| 29 | Services.Utils | Common utilities and helpers used across services. |
| 30 | Services.Validations | Input validation logic for DTOs and custom business rules. |
| 31 | Services.Redis | Redis configuration and caching/locking logic. |
| 32 | Services.EmailClient | Email sending client. |

##### **1.2.3.2 Config Layer Descriptions**

| No | Package | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |

##### **1.2.3.3 App Layer Descriptions**

1.2.3.3 App Layer Descriptions

| No | Package | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 01 | Core | Shared services, utilities, and base classes used across the entire application. It supports all other layers |
| 02 | Data | Data layer handling API interactions and local storage |
| 03 | Domain | Enterprise-wide business rules and is completely independent of any UI, database, or network implementation details |
| 04 | Presentation | Presentation layer with UI components and BLoC implementations. It is what the user sees and interacts with |

##### **1.2.3.4 Core Layer Descriptions**

1.2.3.4 Core Layer Descriptions

| No | Package | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 01 | Base Models | Abstract base classes for models to reduce code duplication |
| 02 | Exception | Custom exception classes for the application |
| 03 | Helpers | A collection of stateless utility functions and extension methods |
| 04 | Network | Network-related configurations |
| 05 | Router | Navigation and routing for the application |
| 06 | Dependency Injections | It configures the dependency injection container |

##### **1.2.3.5 Data Layer Descriptions**

1.2.3.5 Data Layer Descriptions

| No | Package | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 01 | Datasources | The actual source of data. This is typically split into remote and local datasources |
| 02 | Enums | Enumeration definitions |
| 03 | Local Models | Structure of the local database, if it differs from the remote API models |
| 04 | Models | These are Data Transfer Objects that represent the structure of data coming from a specific source |
| 05 | Repositories | Concrete implementations of the Repository Domain interfaces |

1.2.3.6 Domain Layer Descriptions

| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 01 | Use Case | Single, specific business action or user story |
| 02 | Repository Domain | Defines the abstract contracts (interfaces) for the data layer |

1.2.3.7 Presentation Layer Descriptions

| No | Package | Description |

##### **1.2.4.1 App Routing Description**

| No | Package | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 01 | app | The main application folder contains routes and pages. It includes two main areas: auth (Login page) and admin, which contains sub-modules such as device management, kiosk management, workflow management, sync management, and others. Each module contains related pages for performing CRUD operations and configurations. |
| 02 | components  | A shared library containing reusable UI components grouped by domain (e.g., Auth components, Device components, Workflow components, etc.). It also includes shared components such as Form components, Dialog components, Layout components, and Common components. |
| 03 | hooks | Contains custom React hooks used across the application for encapsulating reusable logic, such as data fetching, form handling, and state management. |
| 04 | store | Contains Zustand stores for managing global state across the application, such as user info, shared filters, or UI states. |
| 05 | context | Contains context providers that use React's Context API to manage scoped data like user authentication context, theme settings, or permissions. |
| 06 | service | Contains service modules for handling API calls, usually implemented using axios. These modules abstract the communication between the frontend and the backend. |
| 07 | schema | Holds TypeScript interfaces and schemas to define and validate shared data models used throughout the application. |

##### 

##### **1.2.4.2 Components Package Description**

| No | Package | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 01 | auth | Contains UI components related to authentication flows such as login forms, password fields, and validation messages. |
| 02 | manage-devices  | Components for managing device-related entities like device types, models, and detailed device forms |
| 03 | manage-kiosks | UI components for handling kiosk-related features, such as kiosk type forms and version management interfaces. |
| 04 | manage-workflows | Contains reusable components for creating, updating, and managing workflows. Includes task editors, status selectors, and timeline views. |
| 05 | dialog | Generic dialog or modal components used across the app. Examples include confirmation modals, form dialogs, and information popups. |
| 06 | manage-menus | Components for managing menu items and categories, typically used in applications with ordering features. |
| 07 | manage-syncs | Components for handling data synchronization tasks, sync task logs, schedules, and sync event views. |
| 08 | manage-accounts | Contains UI for account management including profile forms, permission editors, and role selection interfaces. |
| 09 | manage-locations | Components for defining and managing physical locations, such as location pickers, region selectors, and location forms. |
| 10 | manage-orders | UI components for displaying and managing order data such as order details, status tracking, and order item views. |
| 11 | manage-organizations | Components for managing organization information, including company data forms, org unit trees, and permission settings. |
| 12 | manage-products | UI components for managing products: product cards, product form fields, pricing inputs, and inventory-related views. |
| 13 | form | Generic form input components used across all domains, such as text fields, date pickers, toggles, dropdowns, and validation helpers. |
| 14 | common | Shared components that are not domain-specific, including buttons, loading spinners, tags, icons, and typography elements. |
| 15 | layout | Layout-related components such as headers, sidebars, navigation menus, breadcrumbs, and layout wrappers. |
| 16 | manage-stores | UI components for managing store-specific configurations, store listing pages, detail forms, and status indicators. |

##### 

##### **1.2.4.3 Lib Package Description**

| No | Package | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 01 | axios | Provides a centralized configuration of the axios HTTP client. This includes base URL setup, request/response interceptors, token injection (e.g., access token from localStorage), and unified error handling logic. It serves as the foundation for all API communication. |
| 02 | swr | A shared library containing reusable UI components grouped by domain (e.g., Auth components, Device components, Workflow components, etc.). It also includes shared components such as Form components, Dialog components, Layout components, and Common components. |
| 03 | utils | A collection of utility functions and helpers used across the application. These may include formatters (e.g., date, currency), deep clone methods, string manipulation, validation helpers, and other pure functions that increase code reuse and maintainability. |

## **2\. Database Design** {#2.-database-design}

### **2.1. Logical ERD** {#2.1.-logical-erd}

#### ***2.1.1 Automated Brewing Coffee Logical ERD***

![][image6]

### **2.2. Physical ERD** {#2.2.-physical-erd}

#### ***2.2.1 Automated Brewing Coffee Physical ERD***

![][image7]

***Table Descriptions***

| No | Table | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | Accounts | Stores user account information (login, role, status, token, ban/unban). \- Primary keys: AccountId \- Foreign keys: OrganizationId → Organizations.OrganizationId |
| 02 | Organizations | Contains information about organizations (companies using the system). \- Primary keys: OrganizationId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 03 | Stores | Represents stores belonging to an organization. \- Primary keys: StoreId \- Foreign keys: OrganizationId → Organizations.OrganizationId, LocationTypeId → LocationTypes.LocationTypeId |
| 04 | Kiosks | Represents coffee kiosks installed at stores. \- Primary keys: KioskId \- Foreign keys: KioskVersionId → KioskVersions.KioskVersionId, StoreId → Stores.StoreId |
| 05 | KioskTypes | Defines kiosk type categories. \- Primary keys: KioskTypeId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 06 | KioskVersions | Version information of kiosks. \- Primary keys: KioskVersionId \- Foreign keys: KioskTypeId → KioskTypes.KioskTypeId |
| 07 | KioskDeviceMappings | Mapping between kiosks and devices. \- Primary keys: KioskDeviceMappingId \- Foreign keys: DeviceId → Devices.DeviceId, KioskId → Kiosks.KioskId |
| 08 | Devices | Represents a physical device inside a kiosk. \- Primary keys: DeviceId \- Foreign keys: DeviceModelId → DeviceModels.DeviceModelId |
| 09 | DeviceModels | Defines device models with type, manufacturer, etc. \- Primary keys: DeviceModelId \- Foreign keys: DeviceTypeId → DeviceTypes.DeviceTypeId |
| 10 | DeviceTypes | Defines categories/types of devices. \- Primary keys: DeviceTypeId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 11 | DeviceFunctions | Defines functions provided by a device model. \- Primary keys: DeviceFunctionId \- Foreign keys: DeviceModelId → DeviceModels.DeviceModelId |
| 12 | FunctionParameters | Defines parameters of device functions. \- Primary keys: FunctionParameterId \- Foreign keys: DeviceFunctionId → DeviceFunctions.DeviceFunctionId |
| 13 | DeviceIngredients | Defines ingredients a device can use/store. \- Primary keys: DeviceIngredientId \- Foreign keys: DeviceModelId → DeviceModels.DeviceModelId |
| 14 | DeviceIngredientStates | Tracks current state (capacity, refill, etc.) of device ingredients. \- Primary keys: DeviceIngredientStateId \- Foreign keys: DeviceId → Devices.DeviceId |
| 15 | DeviceIngredientHistories | Logs ingredient consumption/refill changes. \- Primary keys: DeviceIngredientHistoryId \- Foreign keys: DeviceIngredientStateId (none explicit), DeviceId → Devices.DeviceId, OrderId → Orders.OrderId |
| 16 | Products | Contains product (drink) information. \- Primary keys: ProductId \- Foreign keys: ProductCategoryId → ProductCategory.ProductCategoryId, ParentId → Products.ProductId |
| 17 | ProductCategory | Defines categories of products (Coffee, Tea, etc.). \- Primary keys: ProductCategoryId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 18 | ProductAttributes | Defines attributes of a product (size, sugar, etc.). \- Primary keys: ProductAttributeId \- Foreign keys: ProductId → Products.ProductId |
| 19 | AttributeOptions | Possible options for product attributes. \- Primary keys: AttributeOptionId \- Foreign keys: ProductAttributeId → ProductAttributes.ProductAttributeId |
| 20 | Menus | Menu owned by an organization. \- Primary keys: MenuId \- Foreign keys: OrganizationId → Organizations.OrganizationId |
| 21 | MenuProductMappings | Mapping between menus and products. \- Primary keys: MenuId, ProductId \- Foreign keys: MenuId → Menus.MenuId, ProductId → Products.ProductId |
| 22 | Orders | Contains orders placed at kiosks. \- Primary keys: OrderId \- Foreign keys: KioskId → Kiosks.KioskId, OrganizationId → Organizations.OrganizationId, StoreId → Stores.StoreId |
| 23 | OrderDetails | Detailed items within an order. \- Primary keys: OrderDetailId \- Foreign keys: OrderId → Orders.OrderId, ProductId → Products.ProductId |
| 24 | Payments | Payment transactions for orders. \- Primary keys: PaymentId \- Foreign keys: OrderId → Orders.OrderId |
| 25 | Workflows | Defines workflows for preparing products. \- Primary keys: WorkflowId \- Foreign keys: ProductId → Products.ProductId, KioskVersionId → KioskVersions.KioskVersionId |
| 26 | Steps | Steps within a workflow. \- Primary keys: StepId \- Foreign keys: WorkflowId → Workflows.WorkflowId, DeviceModelId → DeviceModels.DeviceModelId |
| 27 | Notifications | Stores system notifications. \- Primary keys: NotificationId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 28 | NotificationRecipients | Defines recipients for notifications. \- Primary keys: NotificationRecipientId \- Foreign keys: NotificationId → Notifications.NotificationId, AccountId → Accounts.AccountId |
| 29 | IngredientTypes | Defines types of ingredients (Milk, Sugar, etc.). \- Primary keys: IngredientTypeId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 30 | SystemConfigs | Stores system configuration key-values. \- Primary keys: SystemConfigId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 31 | SyncEvents | Events for syncing across kiosks/clouds. \- Primary keys: SyncEventId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 32 | SyncTasks | Tasks to perform synchronization. \- Primary keys: SyncTaskId \- Foreign keys: SyncEventId → SyncEvents.SyncEventId, KioskId → Kiosks.KioskId |
| 33 | LocationTypes | Defines store location types (Office, Mall, etc.). \- Primary keys: LocationTypeId \- Foreign keys: (none) |
| 34 | Webhooks | Webhook configurations for kiosks. \- Primary keys: WebhookId \- Foreign keys: KioskId → Kiosks.KioskId |

#### ***3.1.3 Class Specification***

##### **3.1.3.1 Auth Controller Description Table**

Figure 3.1.3.1 Auth Controller Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | Login(LoginDto ) | Handles POST requests to authenticate a user using their email and password. If the credentials are valid, return a JWT access token and refresh token. Otherwise, returns an error response with appropriate status code and message. |

##### **3.1.3.2 Auth Service Description Table**

Figure 3.1.3.2 Auth Service Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | Login(LoginDto) | Verifies user credentials. Retrieves the account by email, checks for bans and password correctness, and generates JWT tokens. Stores refresh token either in Redis or falls back to the database. Returns login result as BaseResult\<LoginDto, JwtDto\>. |

##### **3.1.3.2 Auth DTOs Description Table**

Figure 3.1.3.2 Auth Service Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | LoginDto | Data transfer object for login request. Contains Email and Password fields, both marked as required. |
| 02 | JwtDto | Data transfer object returned after successful login. Includes the AccessToken and RefreshToken strings used for authentication and session management. |
| 03 | BaseResult\<TRequest, TResponse\> | A generic wrapper class for API responses. Includes metadata like message, status code, success flag, original request data, and response data. |

### **3.3 Refresh Token** {#3.3-refresh-token}

#### ***3.3.1 Class Diagram***

![][image12]

#### ***3.3.2 Sequence diagram***

![][image13]

#### ***3.3.3 Class Specification***

##### **3.3.3.1 AuthController Description Table**

Figure 3.3.3.1 Auth Controller Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | Refresh(RefreshDto dto) | Handle HTTP POST /auth/refresh; forwards request to AuthService.Refresh() |
| 02 |  |  |

##### **3.3.3.2 AuthService Description Table**

Figure 3.3.3.2 Auth Service Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | Refresh(RefreshDto dto) | Validates refresh token, compares with Redis/DB, and generates new access/refresh tokens |
| 02 | JwtUtil.GetPrincipalFromToken() | Used to extract user claims from refresh token |
| 03 | RedisService.GetDataAsync() | Used to retrieve the currently stored refresh token from Redis |
| 04 | RedisService.SetDataAsync() | Used to update the refresh token in Redis for the account |
| 05 | UnitOfWork.GetRepository\<Account\>() | Fetch account to compare refresh token or update fallback token when Redis is unavailable |

##### **3.3.3.2 JwtUtil Description Table**

Figure 3.3.3.2  JwtUtil Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | GetPrincipalFromToken(string token, IConfiguration config) | Decode and validate refresh token, extract user claims |
| 02 | GenerateAccessToken(Account, IConfiguration) | Create a new short-lived JWT access token |
| 03 | GenerateRefreshToken(Account, IConfiguration) | Generate a new long-lived refresh token |

##### 

##### **3.3.3.3 RedisService Description Table**

Figure 3.3.3.2 Redis ServiceDescription Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | GetDataAsync\<string\>(key) | Retrieve stored refresh token from Redis using key pattern refresh:{id} |
| 02 | SetDataAsync(key, value, expiry) | Save new refresh token in Redis with 7-day TTL |

##### **3.3.3.4 UnitOfWork Description Table**

Figure 3.3.3.2 UnitOfWork DTOs Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | GetRepository\<Account\>() | Access Account repository to read user or update refresh token fallback |
| 02 | CommitAsync() | Persist account token fallback update if Redis fails |

### **3.8 Create Order** {#3.8-create-order}

#### ***3.8.1 Class Diagram***

*![][image22]*

#### ***3.8.2 Sequence diagram***

*![][image23]*

#### ***3.8.3 Class Specification***

##### **3.8.3.1 Order Controller Description Table**

Figure 3.8.3.1 Order Controller Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | Post(CreateOrderDto) | Receives an HTTP POST request to initiate the creation of a new order. It delegates the business logic processing to the IOrderService |

##### **3.8.3.2 Order Service Description Table**

Figure 3.8.3.2 \<name\> Service Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | CreateOrder(CreateOrderDto) | Orchestrates the entire order creation process. This involves calling other methods |
| 02 | CheckIngredientsAvailableAsync() | An internal method to verify if there are enough ingredients in the Kiosk's inventory to fulfill the requested order |
| 03 | Locker.Acquire(key) | Acquires a lock based on a unique key (KioskId) before processing |
| 04 | Locker.Release() | releases lock after processing is complete to ensure data integrity |
| 05 | Repositories.SingleOrDefaultAsync() | Retrieves a single entity (e.g., Kiosk) from the database that matches the specified criteria |
| 06 | Repositories.UpdateRange() | Updates a collection of entities (e.g., DeviceIngredientState) in the database |
| 07 | Repositories.InsertAsync() | Adds a new entity (e.g., Order, Payment) to the database |
| 08 | Mapper.Map() | Transforms an object of one type (e.g., CreateOrderDto) into an object of another type (e.g., Order entity) |
| 09 | PaymentGateways.CreatePaymentUrl() | Communicates with an external payment service (like VNPay or MPOS) to generate a payment URL or QR code |
| 10 | UnitOfWork.CommitAsync() | Saves all changes made within the current transaction (inserts, updates) to the database permanently |

##### **3.8.3.2 Order DTOs Description Table**

Figure 3.8.3.2 \<name\> DTOs Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | CreateOrderDto | A Data Transfer Object used as input. It carries the new order's data from the client to the server, including order details, kiosk ID, and chosen payment method |
| 02 | OrderDto | A Data Transfer Object used as output. It carries the created order's data from the server back to the client, including the new order ID and payment details (URL or QR code) |

### **3.10 Synchronous Kiosk Data**  {#3.10-synchronous-kiosk-data}

#### ***3.10.1 Class Diagram***

*![][image26]*

#### ***3.10.2 Sequence diagram***

*![][image27]*

#### ***3.10.3 Class Specification***

##### **3.10.3.1 Kiosk Sync Controller Description Table**

Figure 3.9.3.1 \<name\> Controller Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | SyncKioskData(SyncActionDto dto) | Receives an HTTP POST request to perform an incremental data synchronization based on specific create, update, or delete actions |
| 02 | SyncOverridenKioskData(OverridenKioskDataSyncDto dto) | Receives an HTTP POST request to perform a full data overwrite, replacing all existing kiosk data with the provided dataset |

##### **3.10.3.2 Kiosk Sync Service Description Table**

Figure 3.9.3.2 \<name\> Service Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | SyncKioskData(SyncActionDto request) | Orchestrates the incremental sync process by delegating entity-specific logic |
| 02 | SyncOverridenKioskData(OverridenKioskDataSyncDto request) | Orchestrates the full data overwrite process by mapping DTOs to domain models and using the appropriate strategy's OverwriteAllAsync method to replace data in the database |
| 03 | ProcessEntitySyncAsync\<TDto, TEntity\>(...) | A generic helper method that processes standard Create, Update, and Delete operations for any given entity type using its corresponding strategy |
| 04 | ProcessStepSyncAsync(EntitySyncOperation\<StepSyncDto\> stepData) | A specialized helper method that handles the unique business logic for syncing Steps by loading the parent Workflow, modifying its internal Steps list, and saving the entire Workflow document |

##### **3.10.3.2 Kiosk Sync DTOs Description Table**

Figure 3.9.3.2 \<name\> DTOs Description Table

| No | Method | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | SyncActionDto, ActionDto, KioskDataSyncDto | A set of nested DTOs used to structure the incremental sync request, with KioskDataSyncDto holding the core CRUD operations |
| 02 | EntitySyncOperation\<T\> | A generic DTO that defines the three possible action lists for an entity: Create, Update, and Delete |
| 03 | OverridenKioskDataSyncDto | A DTO used for the full data overwrite request. It contains complete lists of all entities (a data snapshot) to replace existing data |
| 04 | DeviceSyncDto, WorkflowSyncDto, StepSyncDto | DTOs that represent the data for individual entities (Device, Workflow, Step) being sent from the kiosk |
| 05 | StepConditionRawSyncDto | A DTO that holds the data for a single condition belonging to a Step. It is nested within StepSyncDto |
| 06 | BaseResult | A standard DTO used to encapsulate the result of a service operation, containing a success status, message, and status code |
